findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - the full test suite runs.
This guard also intercepts empty plan-read and intake handbacks. `tests/test_tools_native_reads.py:85-89,109-110` still expects the read lane to be released and the read to fail; `tests/test_start_sorts_ideas.py:136-140` expects an empty explorer reply to produce a successful retry nudge. Both tests will fail under the new guard, leaving their remaining lifecycle checks unrun. Update both tests for the intended retry behavior.
findings.title: Gate: read and intake tests still expect the old empty-message behavior

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an explorer finishes without answering.
The guard runs before the intake retry nudge in `src/forge/intake.py:78-87`. `plans/FORGE-INTAKE-1.md:125-131` explicitly identifies an empty reply as a model that did not answer. In that case, the printed instruction asks for a last message that does not exist; following it repeats the refusal while the place remains held. This is distinct from the committed-build case in the coordinator's ruling. Tell the coordinator to obtain a reply from the explorer before retrying.
Adds work: ask the explorer to produce a reply; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Request a new reply when the explorer produced no message

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a Codex coordinator retries an empty build handback.
The new regression test forces a Claude session, while the changed build lifecycle test removes its former empty-handback case for both tools. No test checks that a Codex build round retains its hold and accepts the retry, so the tests could pass if that path still failed or released the round. The repo's same-result rule requires the behavior tests through both adapters.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_empty_handback_preserves_round_for_message_retry on Codex

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - Forge records an informational event when refusing a handback.
The test compares the complete internal event and timing files byte for byte and later parses their JSON fields. An informational event or storage-only refactor would fail this test even if the round stayed open and was never marked failed. Check the visible round and board state at the command boundary instead, as the test-audit rule requires.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_empty_handback_preserves_round_for_message_retry uses private records

stop.reason: Harm 3 findings: one more round by the standing rule

why: When forge handback gets no message, it records the round as failed and its next step says forge work, which restarts a round whose work is already committed, instead of saying to hand back again with the message
